The next fix or change to pagination logic must be applied in two places and they have already drifted within this diff (the prev-page trim condition is wrong on the negative-offset path it was written for); maintainers of the shared paginator will miss the copy.
records.rationale: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, the negative-offset branch slices with `start_offset = cursor.offset` and `stop = start_offset + limit + extra`, but the later prev-page trim logic still checks `elif len(results) == offset + limit + extra:` where `offset` is the raw (possibly negative) `cursor.offset` (see `offset = cursor.offset`). On the negative-offset path this makes the trim condition inconsistent with the slice window (RHS can be smaller/negative), so the “drop the extra row” behavior for `cursor.is_prev` can fail, leading to incorrect page boundaries/duplicate or missing items.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The Lua script now calls zcard/zunionstore on keys that old-code instances are still writing as sets, and Redis raises WRONGTYPE on a type-command mismatch, aborting the script. In the deploy window where an old pod sadds span-buf:s:* and a new pod's script zcard's the same key, the script fails, the span insert is rejected, and buffered traces stop joining until all old pods are gone.
records.rationale: Diff changes Redis data structure for `span-buf:s:{...}:<id>` from SET to ZSET: Python writes with `p.zadd(set_key, {span.payload: span.end_timestamp_precise ...})` instead of `p.sadd(...)` (src/sentry/spans/buffer.py), and Lua now reads/merges with `zcard`/`zunionstore` and trims with `zpopmin` (src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua) instead of `scard`/`sunionstore`. There is no compatibility/migration handling for pre-existing keys of the old type. In a rolling deploy, keys created by old code as SETs but still within TTL will cause `zcard`/`zunionstore` in the Lua script to raise WRONGTYP

records.issue_text: [BUG] The new eviction path zpopmin's set_key down to 1000 members, silently deleting buffered spans with no backup, logging, or metric. For any trace segment exceeding 1000 spans, the oldest-end-timestamp spans are permanently dropped before the segment is ever flushed, so customers with large traces lose span data with zero observability.
records.rationale: In `src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua`, the new cap enforcement evicts entries via `zpopmin(set_key, span_count - 1000)` (lowest score = earliest `end_timestamp_precise`). records.issue_text: [BUG] process_batch reads the new required field via val["end_timestamp_precise"] against messages produced by the current schema version, with no .get() fallback for the pre-existing Kafka backlog. On deploy, the consumer processing already-queued messages lacking end_timestamp_precise raises KeyError, the batch is never committed, and the consumer stalls in a crash loop until offsets are manually skipped — those spans are lost.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The redirect-loop depth limit is silently reduced from 10000 to 1000 with no data-dependent migration step, so segment trees deeper than 1000 are no longer joined. Traces with redirect chains between depth 1000 and 10000 that previously joined correctly now split into multiple segments, silently degrading those customers' trace data after deploy.

records.issue_text: [BUG] `val["end_timestamp_precise"]` raises KeyError for any span event where the optional field is absent, crashing the whole batch. end_timestamp_precise is not guaranteed on every ingest_spans_v1 message (producers that omit it are valid); process_batch raises, the RunTask strategy fails, and the consumer stalls on the partition — spans from the entire batch are dropped rather than just the offending span, and the pipeline backs up with no per-span error surfaced.
records.rationale: below CONF_FLOOR (0.45)

records.issue_text: [BUG] `redis.call("zcard", span_key)` / `zunionstore` on keys written as plain sets by the pre-deploy `sadd` code raises WRONGTYPE during a rolling deploy. Keys `span-buf:s:{...}:span_id` written by the old process_spans `p.sadd` path are Redis sets; after deploy the new Lua script calls zcard/zunionstore on them, the script errors, and every span for that trace fails to be buffered (ingest dropped) until the legacy keys expire. Same skew hits the new `zscan` in buffer.py:_load_segment_data against old-format keys, breaking segment flushing mid-deploy.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The 'advanced' negative-offset path slices a Django queryset with a negative start (`queryset[start_offset:stop]` with start_offset < 0), which Django rejects with 'Negative indexing is not supported'. Any request with a crafted/hand-built cursor carrying a negative offset on the optimized path raises AssertionError inside the ORM and returns a 500, where the comment claims 'the underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' — it does not for querysets, so the advertised feature cannot ever execute successfully and the endpoint 500s instead of returning results or a 4xx for an invalid cursor.
records.rationale: below CONF_FLOOR (0.45)

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] zpopmin silently evicts the 1000+ oldest spans from the segment set with no log, no metric, and the has_root_span flag still set, so the segment flushes as success with silently truncated data. Large segments (e.g. traces with >1000 spans) get their earliest-end_timestamp spans dropped; the flushed segment is emitted as a complete success while missing data, and operators get zero signal (the accompanying removal of the max_segment_spans guard in buffer.py also deleted the segment_span_count_exceeded metric, leaving only the byte-size signal). The evicted members can also include the boundary spans a later zscan-based rebuild depends on.

records.issue_text: [BUG] `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` passes a negative offset straight into `queryset[start_offset:stop]` for prev cursors, raising the ORM's negative-indexing AssertionError. A crafted prev-cursor with a negative offset value hits `queryset[-N:...]`, Django raises 'Negative indexing is not supported', and the endpoint returns a 500 instead of a 4xx for a malformed cursor.
records.rationale: below CONF_FLOOR (0.45)
